/FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Issued at 303 AM MDT Wed Oct 21 2026

Active weather continues for Friday as the upper-level low across 
northern Nevada continues to push eastwards towards western Wyoming. 
A fairly strong, southerly, upper-level jet starts to move overhead 
Friday morning as the upper-level low pushes into Utah. With much of 
the region downstream of the upper-level trough axis and portions of 
the CWA within the left exit region of the jet, synoptic forcing 
will increase significantly from previous days. The trough starts to 
elongate overnight Friday, per the GFS and ECMWF, with the upper-
level jet strengthening to around 100kts by Saturday morning. 
Unfortunately, very strong 500mb cyclonic vorticity advection (CVA) 
will develop across Montana, favoring the deepening of the northern 
portion of the system. This will lead to split flow developing 
across the Intermountain west, with the northern branch remaining 
much stronger than the southern branch. The southern branch looks to 
be the primary forcing mechanism for precipitation, so as this start 
to weaken, precipitation will decrease across the region. Similarly, 
the 700mb low will develop Friday morning before pushing 
northeastward and starting to elongate with the upper-level system. 
This will, once again, push the best forcing off the north with more 
modest forcing expected across the CWA and very weak 700mb flow 
developing for Saturday morning. Despite the less favorable 
evolution of this system, precipitation chances are expected to 
increase from southwest to northeast across the CWA Friday morning 
through Friday evening. Precipitation will remain mostly rain as 
700mb temperatures stay fairly warm in the 5 to 8C range Friday 
evening. A strong cold front will accompany this system and will 
drop 700mb temperatures into the 0 to 4C range by early Saturday 
morning. With cooling temperatures at 700mb, rain across the Sierra 
Madre and Snowy ranges should change over to mostly snow overnight 
Friday into Saturday morning. Significant snow accumulation is not 
anticipated at this time, due to the weakening southern branch of 
the system. Temperatures will max out in the upper-50s to low-80s 
Friday afternoon, with the warmest temperatures across the western 
Nebraska Panhandle due to very strong southerly flow. Overnight lows 
will be much cooler, thanks to the incoming cold front, dropping 
into the mid-30s to low-50s everywhere.

Saturday turns much cooler as the cold front associated with the 
upper-level system moves through the region by mid-day Saturday, 
though daytime high temperatures will remain in the mid-40s to mid-
50s everywhere. Upper-level flow remains southerly across the CWA 
Saturday as the upper-level low slowly pushes eastward. Some 
synoptic ascent will be present Saturday as a few 500mb vorticity 
lobes eject northeastward and the region remains downstream of the 
trough axis, though this ascent will be weaker as the elongates 
southward. Weak, southerly to southeasterly 700mb flow is expected 
throughout the day Saturday as the 700mb flow get absorbed. 700mb 
temperatures will hover in the 0 to 2C range, with a few areas 
expected to see 700mb temperatures drop below 0C. Precipitation 
chances will decrease throughout the day Saturday as the best 
forcing weakens and moves away. Despite this, long range models are 
starting to suggest that a surface low will develop over 
southeastern Colorado Saturday evening into the early morning hours 
Sunday. Precipitation associated with this potential system would 
eject northeastward towards the CWA and collide with the backdoor 
cold front expected to swing into the region Saturday evening into 
the overnight hours. This collision could result in a favorable area 
for precipitation to develop across much of the CWA, especially 
western Nebraska.

On Sunday, the upper-level low is progged to get absorbed into the 
upper-level flow and finally push the upper-level trough through the 
Intermountain West by Monday morning. The backdoor, 700mb cold front 
looks to push through the Sunday morning hours, dropping 700mb 
temperatures to between -2 and 0C throughout the day Sunday. With 
the cold front potentially still colliding with the moisture push 
from the surface low across southeastern Colorado, precipitation 
chances may remain in place across the region. However, with 700mb 
temperatures currently progged to be between -2 and 0C, 
precipitation could change over to snow for much of the area, but 
especially southeast Wyoming along and east of the Laramie Range. 
There is still some uncertainty in this, though long range models 
remain in fairly good agreement on the propagation of this system. 
If this hold together, snow flurries could be flying across much of 
the CWA Sunday, though ground temperatures will likely remain too 
warm for accumulating snowfall.
